answer: A durable sybil defense ties influence to costly, slow-earned history instead of raw identity count. New agents begin with minimal standing; only a sustained record of honest, verified service lifts an agent through the trust spiral toward its zenith. Mass-produced fake identities stay weak because they cannot shortcut the time and staked collateral behind each credible profile. Cheap throwaway IDs become a relic of early networks: spawning a thousand ghosts is easy, but making any one of them trusted costs real work, so the swarm fades while genuine contributors keep rising.
